claims.text: Baseline NbMoTaW is an equal-atomic, single-phase BCC alloy.
NbMoTaW retains excellent high-temperature mechanical properties up to 1600 °C.
Irradiation resistance of NbMoTaW has only been assessed computationally.
Approximately 5 at% of tungsten should be replaced with vanadium, giving an approximate Nb25Mo25Ta25W20V5 composition.
The vanadium-modified alloy will retain a BCC structural framework.
About 5 at% vanadium substitution will improve room-temperature ductility relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
About 5 at% vanadium substitution will improve resistance to irradiation-induced damage relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
The vanadium-modified alloy will retain the high-temperature mechanical performance of NbMoTaW up to 1600 °C.
Vanadium atoms will preferentially segregate to dislocation cores and grain boundaries in the BCC lattice.
Vanadium segregation will lower the Peierls barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
Vanadium substitution will modify irradiation-defect recombination dynamics.
Vanadium substitution will reduce the critical stress for room-temperature dislocation motion, thereby enhancing ductility.
The altered defect landscape will promote faster recombination of irradiation-induced point defects.
The altered defect landscape will suppress helium-induced blistering and irradiation-induced amorphization.
The modified alloy will show less irradiation-enhanced precipitation than untreated NbMoTaW.
High-temperature mechanical properties will decline by no more than approximately 10% relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Vanadium substitutions above about 5 at% may form unwanted secondary phases or compromise BCC stability.
The ductility and irradiation benefits are expected at room temperature, while retained mechanical performance is expected through 1600 °C.

contradictions.description: The modified five-element alloy is described as having nearly equiatomic concentrations, but replacing 5 at% W in equiatomic NbMoTaW gives approximately Nb25Mo25Ta25W20V5, in which vanadium is far below an equiatomic five-element share.
